content: Goal: write the mathematics of the chosen mechanism (behaviour-directed geodesic code drift, levels 2-3). First step: inspect the workspace for the geometry contract and the contract module so every operator can be quoted exactly, not re-derived. Still open: whether the spec is complete enough (lift, log map, mobius add, distance, sinkhorn plan) or must be declared SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE.

Goal: fix the operator conventions before writing any formula. Read: the workspace (only progress.jsonl exists, so the geometry module itself is not available) and the embedded hyperbolc geometry contract poincare-contract/v1 in the task. Observed/derived: (a) the spec's lift v_i = (1/sqrt(c)) tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q_l) r/||r|| is EXACTLY the contract's exp_0^c(r/q_l) = tanhc(sqrt(c)||r||/q_l)(r/q_l) - so the lift is a contract operator, not a new one; (b) the displacement (1/sqrt(c)) tanh(sqrt(c) m_i/2) n_i is exp_0^c((m_i/2) n_i), and by contract identity 4, d_c(0, exp_0(v)) = 2||v||, so its origin distance is 2*(m_i/2) = m_i, i.e. the half-factor in the spec is exactly the contract's factor-2 tangent normalisation, NOT an error; (c) the spec's d_P(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(...) omits the contract's factor 2, so the authority d_c = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(clip(sqrt(c)||(-x)(+)y||, 0, 1-1e-5)) must be quoted instead; (d) the log map must carry 2/(sqrt(c) lambda_x), and zero norms go through tanhc/atanhc limits, never 1e-12. Still open: whether the GEOM=euclid branch and the gradient path through C are well defined; check next.

Goal: test the spec for internal consistency before deciding complete vs SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE. Observed, four real defects: (1) GEOM=euclid does not match the contract's c->0 limit: the lift's limit is v = r/q_l (a linear map, NOT the 'bounded Euclidean radial map' the spec claims), the displacement's limit is (m_i/2) n_i, and the contract fixes d_0 = 2||x-y||, whereas the spec writes C = ||(v_i - u_k) - m_i n_i||_2 - wrong by a factor 2 in the displacement and a factor 2 in the metric, with no rule for the lift. (2) ||t_i|| is unstated: Euclidean coordinate norm of the tangent vector or the Riemannian norm lambda_{v_i}||t_i|| required by contract section 3; m_i and Delta_i scale with it. (3) The total loss is declared to be the baseline RQ-VAE loss on the ASSIGNED codes and the decoder receives the chosen raw codeword, so the plan is turned into an index (no gradient) and C never reaches the loss - which contradicts 'gradients flow through v_i and u_k only' unless an auxiliary term in C or P exists; no such term or coefficient is given. (4) the level-3 snapshot content (which level-2 codes define r_{s,3}, and whether the snapshot uses epoch-start or current assignments) and the empty-successor case W_i = 0 are undefined; also unstated whether the 0.5*d_nn clamp inside m_i is detached (only t_i and n_i are declared detached). Decision: write the full mathematics of every defined piece and mark incomplete = SPECIFICATION_INCOMPLETE with these items in missing. Next: append the complete answer block.

The train-split directed successor multiset of item i, read from a per-epoch detached ball-point snapshot V_l, gives a tangent behaviour vector t_i = sum_s (w_is/W_i) log_{v_i}^c(V_l[s]) at v_i; its unit direction n_i and its length M_i fix an arc length m_i = min(M_i, 0.5*min_k d_c(v_i,u_k)), identically 0 when BEHAV=off. Every code is then displaced inside the ball along the item's direction, q_{i,k} = u_k (+) exp_0^c((m_i/2) n_i), a Mobius translation by a ball element whose origin distance is exactly m_i, and the cost C[i,k] = d_c(v_i, q_{i,k}) is the exact Poincare distance from the item point to the displaced code. C is fed unchanged into the baseline entropy-regularised Sinkhorn with the baseline epsilon, uniform item marginal and balanced code marginal; the plan P is kept (no argmin of C replaces it), the baseline plan extraction turns P into indices, the decoder is fed the chosen raw codeword through the baseline straight-through estimator, and the baseline RQ-VAE loss trains encoder and codebook. Behaviour enters only as a detached, once-per-epoch field; c = 0 is the contract's Euclidean limit branch.
